post_title: how to leather fabric edge wax

comments.comment_body: Hi 19483261409561, My first try would be adding an image at an edge as either a topstitch or a graphic and set the Material Type to reflect in a way that it looks waxy by editing Reflection Intensity and Roughness.
how to crate graphic for wax look?

Hi 19483261409561, With a topstitch set to Texture instead of OBJ, it will be easiest, as it will follow the shape of the line it is placed on as a repeat. You only need a small square image, for example (in this case maybe blurred a bit on the edge facing inside the pattern piece). Please see these videos for advanced topstitch application: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZncCv3ijsZM&ampt=813s and here https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ypI_SPLxLFY

You really need to use texture masks on the pattern UV in a texture paint application to get get that worn wax grunge bleed at the stitch and seam edges. It's not something you can simply tile in a linear edge as the dirt is a blend of how the shine (reflectivity texture channel) is changed on the suede. And then the height map might also be slightly smoother (worn) in these areas. I suggest you create your garment model and then export the UV and pattern layouts to a texture paint application &gt bake a basic suede fabric to the albedo, normal, height, reflectivity, etc texture maps &gt then open up in a texture paint application and add in the wax/wear and tear by baking some extra texture maps to paint in the wax and wear just where you need it. Then reimport those UV atlas maps back into CLO3D and render in vray. Only way to do it comprehensively.

post_details: Hi everyone, Please help me on this case, I'm trying to figure out how to make the bottom seam display as the chain stitch like this, which properties do I have to change? Many thanks!

comments.comment_body: So the right hand image is your workspace, correct? It looks like the waistband is a double layer and the layers are back to back, as they would be IRL. The chainstich provided with CLO is set up for a single layer waistband where the chain is only stitch 2 and is placed on the back. That's fine for your outer band, but you want to swap those for the inner band. You probably will use both configurations, so first make a copy. E.g. here's one way, this is a folded waistband, with regular chainstitch applied to the front half, and reversed chainstitch applied to the back half. This may not be the way you want to do it, but it should help explain how topstitching works with fronts and backs. (This is overkill because it is placing topstitching on the backs of each layer, too.)

post_details: I see no instructions for setting a pattern piece's grainline to 4 ways (or no grainline). I see a 4 way grain setting in the print layout function (property editor), however, setting that to 4 way does not actually rotate any pieces to more efficiently nest. Do I set 2 grainlines for each piece (one horizontal, one vertical)? Do I need to select a fabric with no grain, a non-woven? Do I simply delete the grain lines? comments.comment_body: Hi 13748879622041, Grainlines are connected to the pattern pieces and will remain the way they are set regardless of fabric changes. Any texture rotation you do regarding the maps on a fabric are separate from the grainlines. It is not possible to completely delete out a grainline from a pattern piece or have multiple grainlines on the same piece. There will always be an angle and the default is 0. You can edit the grainline manually with the Edit Texture tool by clicking on and rotating only on the pattern piece in question (instead of using the flat black gizmo for entire map rotation), or selecting a pattern piece and editing the grainline with precise input in the Property Editor.

post_details: 아바타에 모션(노핸즈, 드레스, 한복 등 모드)을 적용 후 스테이지에서 아바타가 런웨이 시 손이나 다리 등에 원단이 통과가 되고, 흔들림이 너무 심해 의상이 제대로 영상 안에 담기지 않습니다. 이를 해결하기 위해 원단의 사전물성을 머슬린으로 바꿔보기도 하고, 원단 패턴의 길이감을 줄여 끌리지 않게도 해봤으며, 아바타의 시침 혹은 원단과 원단 사이에 시침 등의 툴을 이용해 고정을 시키기도 했습니다. 많은 방법들을 시도해봤지만 해결하지 못했습니다. clo에 자문을 구하고 싶어 문의글을 올립니다. 감사합니다.

comments.comment_body: 안녕하세요. 해당 파일을 직접 확인하여 보지 못해 정확한 답변을 드릴 순 없겠지만, 애니메이션 시 참고하시면 좋을 간단한 몇가지 팁을 아래와 같이 드립니다. 해당 팁은 절대적인 것은 아니며 참고 정도로 활용 하시면 좋을 것 같습니다. 1. 패턴에 레이어 설정이 되어 있다면 0으로 해주세요. 2. 패턴의 충돌 두께 값을 2.5로 설정 해주세요. 3. 적용된 원단의 물성 중 internal damping 값을 0.00001 혹은 이하로 해주세요. 4. 입자간격은 8 또는 10으로 해주세요. 5. 아바타 클릭 후 속성창에서 Kinetic friction 값을 0.3, 0.5 또는 1.0으로 해주세요.
5가지 전부 적용했는데도 계속 손에 의상이 부딪혀 옷이 이상하게 뒤틀립니다ㅠ 모션도 그냥 기본 캣워크 모션인데..어떻게 하면 되나요?

안녕하세요. 지난번 답변 드린 사항에 더불어 아래의 항목도 시도 해보시면 좋을 것 같습니다. 1. 아바타 클릭 후 속성창에서 skin offset(mm)을 3mm~5mm로 해주세요. 2. 애니메이션 모드에 진입 후 애니메이션 프레임 창에 있는 Scene time warp 값을 2로 늘려주신 후 의상 녹화를 진행 해주세요. 녹화가 완료 된 후에 다시 1로 줄여주시면 됩니다. *scene time warp : 모션의 프레임 수를 scene time warp 값 만큼 곱하여 늘리거나 줄여줍니다. 따라서 문의 주신 상황과 같은 경우 전체 프레임 수를 늘려줘서 프레임 당 시뮬레이션 계산 횟수를 늘려줌으로써 좀 더 안정적인 의상 녹화가 가능 하도록 해줍니다. 다만, 프레임 수가 늘어난 만큼 녹화 시간도 늘어나고, 전체 파일의 개수도 늘어나기 때문에 녹화 후 값을 1로 줄여주시면 됩니다.

post_details: Hello, For a current project i want to automatically generate 100 000 images of a hoody as training data for a neural network. The images have the following constraints: - The distance to the "camera" needs to be the same for every picture - the position of the hoody for each image can change as follows: - arms change position randomly between images - y-axis rotation of the hoody changes randomly between images - the position needs to be realistic (no arms going through the center of the hoody for example) Is this possible to implement in CLO3D?

comments.comment_body: Hi 360528923247 While we believe you have already gotten some excellent feedback from out Discord channel. But keep in mind that CLO currently only renders 1 image at a time. And if you were to render 100,000 images at 1 minutes an image this would take your computer 69 days to complete. And the 1 minute would be for an image at a medium quality and the garment would not be overly complex or using any Render only materials. If you had a complex garment, detailed textures, and a high resolution the average image would take much longer. So while CLO may be ideal for building the garment it may not be ideal for rendering this large of a number of images

post_details: So the Tutorial Creator in this Youtube Video explained that we need to change the maximum value of stress and strain of the fabric in the Garment Properties Dialog Box. For the software to analyze the fit. By default the Maximum values are fixed for Stress at 100kPa and for strain to be 120%. This is for all the fabrics that are given for free in clo. So, if a fabric is more or less stretchy we would need to know the maximum value of the particular material to get the perfect fit analysis. My question is how to know the max stress and strain value of my fabric? Would I need an experimental setup? I interacted with Clo in the comments of the video and they seem to suggest that if we use Clo fabric kit, it would automatically calculate the max value of the stress and strain. But if this was the case why are these values constant for all the free fabrics in clo? They must have digitized the fabrics using a fabric kit right?

comments.comment_body: Hi 390325627753, The values that CLO knows through fabric digitizing via the kit and emulator refer to stretch values within the fabric file. The garment fit maps serve only the purpose of visualization since fabric cannot rip in CLO. Changing values in the Garment Fit Properties is an option if you wish to express more visual detail in the maps for either quite stretchy or quite stiff materials. It is not a must to edit them.
